A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConTextTab research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, architectural and training ablations, and dataset-size analyses in Tables 1–3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds semantic ablations, runtime measurements and expanded baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The semantic encoders, interleaved attention, prediction heads, bagging, binning, clustering and ISAB procedures remain. Added layer-normalization details and revised weight-sharing wording clarify the implementation without establishing an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: The pretraining corpora and all 203 prediction-task inventory entries remain unchanged, including their row counts, column counts and target types. Appendix A.3 adds synthetic mixed categorical/textual and numerical tables for runtime evaluation, modestly extending test coverage.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates TabM across the benchmarks and Mambular on CARTE and TALENT-Tiny. Tables 1 and 3 also add previously missing comparisons, including TabICL on OpenML-CC18 and TabReD and RealMLP-HPO on TabReD. ModernNCA is added only as related work.

E3.justification: v3 adds five-fold inner-CV ensembles, changes baseline HPO search spaces to TabArena, and switches CatBoost evaluation from GPU to CPU. Section 4.2 also replaces raw regression-score aggregation with soft-clipping of negative R2 values. Semantic-input controls and a single-query runtime protocol are added; the outer 70/10/20 split remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The original ablation groups are retained. v3 adds direct tests replacing semantic feature encodings with ordinal, MinHash, Gap and AutoGluon encodings, plus column-name removal and description enrichment (Section 5.1, Table 2). Appendix A.3 additionally compares prediction and fitting runtimes as table size increases.

E5.justification: v1 already reports a critical-difference diagram and bootstrapped 80% confidence bands. v3 adds systematic pairwise p-value reporting, including two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests by benchmark and for semantic ablations, and reports five-repeat runtime averages. This substantially expands statistical reporting without establishing additional pretraining runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3 contain extensive replacements and additions. Under the revised comparison, ConTextTab's overall mean rank changes from 2.20 to 2.96, while RealMLP-HPO-CV leads at 2.50; changed comparators and settings prevent interpreting this as same-setting deterioration. New semantic results include losses of 1.2 accuracy and 2.1 R2 percentage points when column names are removed. Runtime results and previously missing baseline scores are also added.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 introduces a modified score definition: negative R2 values are transformed by tanh, while nonnegative values remain unchanged, with stated ordering and smoothness properties. The clustering loss, ISAB equation, binning mathematics and Chebyshev argument remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The semantic-ICL contribution remains, but the conclusion narrows broad SOTA and ICL-superiority language to competitiveness on non-semantic benchmarks and superiority on CARTE. Section 5 withdraws the statistically significant best-overall-ranking claim and acknowledges stronger overall ranking from ensembled RealMLP.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of embedding overhead and attention-related runtime scaling, distinguishes prediction latency from fitting cost, and identifies effective ICL ensembling as an open challenge. It also replaces the conclusion's TabDPT evaluation-failure explanation with a conjecture about its row-based architecture. Most contamination, data-diversity and scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the default 8192-row inference context, embedding layer normalization, feedforward width and parameter counts. It updates baseline package versions and hardware information and documents Gemma3-12b column-description generation from five JSON-serialized rows. These refine existing reproducibility information; the code/checkpoint access location is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to TabM, ModernNCA, Mambular, TabArena and work on benchmarking tables containing text, while removing the Grinsztajn et al. 2022 reference. These update baseline and benchmarking context without substantially redefining the paper's semantic foundation-model positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language corrections, revises the results narrative, reformats author information and adds acknowledgements. Runtime analysis receives its own subsection, further ablations move from A.3 to A.4, and experimental details move from Appendix B to C. The main section sequence and much existing prose remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn; comparison tables are expanded and reordered; Table 2 gains a third ablation group. New or expanded displays include p-value matrices, benchmark-specific critical-difference diagrams, runtime curves, semantic-ablation plots, an attention-block diagram and a datatype-summary table. The existing dataset inventory and dataset-size scatterplot are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses two important weaknesses: v1 did not directly isolate the value of feature and header semantics, and its broad superiority claim relied on weaker comparisons. The new semantic controls, stronger baselines and narrower conclusions substantially improve empirical support and claim calibration. Statistical comparisons and runtime measurements further clarify practical tradeoffs. Soft-clipped R2 compresses severe regression failures and complicates cross-version comparison, but this disclosed tradeoff does not outweigh the gains.
